s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic systemic illness with fever, weight loss, and localized inflammatory lesions
salient_findings: Progressively worsening fever, weight loss, night sweats, and dry cough
Painful nonhealing ulcer on the right hallux
Chronic lower back pain with tenderness over the thoracic spine
Necrotizing granulomatous inflammation on biopsy of the toe ulcer
Bilateral reticular-nodular opacities on chest radiograph
key_facts: Negative sputum GeneXpert tests at local clinics
Symptomatic treatment with paracetamol, NSAIDs, and topical antibacterials
No lymphadenopathy or edema on examination
Negative ANA, anti-dsDNA, ANCA, HIV, hepatitis B and C, and syphilis serologies
Induced sputum trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert
MTB sensitive to rifampicin and isoniazid on culture
Biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus
MRI of the spine revealed contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection causing spinal cord compression

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Induced sputum trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert and subsequent culture growth of MTB, biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic systemic illness with fever, weight loss, and localized inflammatory lesions, granulomatous inflammation on biopsy

shortlist.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Necrotizing granulomatous inflammation on biopsy, renal involvement with hematuria and proteinuria

shortlist.label: Brucellosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic fever, weight loss, and localized inflammatory lesions, although less likely given the biopsy and culture results

shortlist.label: Sjögren's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic systemic illness with fever and localized inflammatory lesions, although less likely given the lack of specific symptoms like dry eyes or mouth

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and test results, including a 2-year history of progressively worsening fever, weight loss, night sweats, and a dry cough, along with a trace positive sputum GeneXpert test and subsequent growth of MTB sensitive to rifampicin and isoniazid, strongly support the diagnosis of tuberculosis. Additionally, the biopsy of the toe ulcer showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus further confirms this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: While sarcoidosis can cause granulomatous inflammation, the presence of acid-fast bacilli and positive MTB culture point more strongly towards tuberculosis.

rejected.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a combination of respiratory and renal symptoms, but the lack of ANCA positivity and the presence of MTB make tuberculosis a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Brucellosis
rejected.why: Brucellosis can cause similar systemic symptoms, but the positive MTB culture and GeneXpert test, as well as the biopsy findings, make tuberculosis a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sjögren's syndrome
rejected.why: This condition primarily affects the exocrine glands and does not typically present with the combination of symptoms and test results seen in this patient, making tuberculosis a more likely diagnosis.
